Bev Craig said funding would be made available to all of the boroughs and it would be enough to repair and maintain over a million square metres of road. Craig had promised to repair more roads and make sure pavements were safe during her election campaign. But Rod Dennis from the RAC said what was needed to fix "Britain's pothole woes, and those we see in Manchester, is guaranteed long-term funding over many, many years". Image caption, Funding is being made available to all 10 Greater Manchester boroughs Dennis called for "an end to the kind of patch and dash approach which we've seen some councils employ and proper planning to get the roads back to where they need to be". Craig said 2.5 billion journeys were made across the roads of Greater Manchester every year "and we need to properly invest in them and this is about getting money out of the door quickly to fix the things that people have been complaining to me about". title: Wigan mum tells of son's sepsis ordeal that left him in coma

evidence_packet.title: Wigan mum tells of son's sepsis ordeal that left him in coma
evidence_packet.lead: Archie's family say their lives changed overnight after he became seriously unwell at the age of five
evidence_packet.summary: Archie's family say their lives changed overnight after he became seriously unwell at the age of five
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mother has told how her family's lives changed over night when her son developed life-threatening sepsis at the age of five Archie, from Wigan, Greater Manchester, was diagnosed with meningitis B which developed into sepsis , external and he spent five days in a coma in 2018 He was admitted to the paediatric intensive care unit at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital, where he received specialist care and rehabilitation before being discharged two weeks later His mother Kate said her son's illness "changed our lives overnight" and seeing him "so seriously unwell and fighting for his life was the most frightening time we have ever experienced as a family" Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to infection anywhere in the body, where, instead of fighting the bacteria or virus that is making you ill, the immune system turns on itself, damaging internal organs and potentially causing death Now aged 13, Archie continues to receive care at the hospital, attending for regular check-ups, undergoing operations, and receiving physiotherapy and occupational therapy

title: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks

evidence_packet.title: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks
evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police dismisses six officers over racial language used against a colleague
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Six Greater Manchester Police officers sacked over racist remarks - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Six officers were sacked without notice by Greater Manchester Police. By Paul Burnell Reporting from North West Published 2 September 2026 Six serving police officers have been sacked following an internal investigation by Greater Manchester Police into alleged racial discrimination against a fellow officer. GMP said two other former officers who were also investigated would have been fired if they were still on the force. Another officer received written warning. A force disciplinary panel heard the female officer of African heritage (who was not named in the proceedings) complained after her accent was mimicked by a group of officers. She was also compared to a suspect with similar skin colour, while one officer made a derogatory comment about her hair. The panel found six officers and two former officers committed gross misconduct, while a ninth officer was found to have committed misconduct. PCs Demi Green, Heena Rani, Lucy Granby, Matthew Barlow, Matthew Hill, and Mohammed Abid - who made the remark about his colleague's hair - were dismissed without notice. Former PC Jake Holt and another unidentified former officer were also found to have committed gross misconduct. Sgt Adrian Bick, whose actions amounted to misconduct, but who did not breach the force's standard of equality and diversity, received a written warning. Deputy chief constable Terry Woods said: "No officer or member of staff should have to come to work and experience discriminatory behaviour from the people they serve alongside. "I would like to acknowledge the courage of the officer who came forward and reported these concerns. It is important that people have the confidence to speak up

evidence_packet.summary: Allie Pottinger painted a mural for a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room
evidence_packet.evidence_text: I want to give comfort to grieving families, says artist - BBC News Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, Artist Allie Pottinger, with Mandy and Josh Ogden of the Georgia Leigh Ogden Foundation, stand in front of the new mural By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 2 September 2026 An artist who has painted a mural in a hospital maternity unit's bereavement room said she "just wanted to bring some comfort" to heartbroken families after the loss of a baby. Allie Pottinger created the mural at Macclesfield General Hospital's Bluebell Suite, described as a private and peaceful space where families can begin to grieve and spend time together. She said she chose the painting of bluebell woods for its calming properties and solace featuring a gate showing light "to offer some hope". It is the watercolour artist's fourth painting in the hospital, which has a special place in her heart. Her late father was a consultant surgeon for 22 years and her sister also now works there. Image source, East Cheshire NHS Trust Image caption, Allie Pottinger's first mural - in memory of her father - depicted Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast She said she painted her first two murals at the hospital - of Shutlingsloe on the edge of Macclesfield Forest and Porth Diana at Trearddur Bay on the Anglesey coast - with her dad in mind in 2022, the year after his death. "I wanted to gift something because he lived and breathed it," said the 60-year-old artist. She said: "Nature is very calming - and it is better than looking at white blank walls." Pottinger, who grew up in Macclesfield but now lives in Congleton, said it was "really rewarding" to paint murals at the hospital. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Four more people have been charged with arson in connection with a wildfire The blaze at Dove Stone reservoir, near Greenfield, Saddleworth, Greater Manchester, broke out on 11 July and was declared a major incident by the fire service. It took more than three weeks to extinguish Tyler Warburton, 18, Toby Wilde, 18, Jake Eyre, 19, and Lyreec Bryan-Gavin, 22, are all accused of arson with recklessness as to whether life was endangered and have all been bailed ahead of their scheduled court appearance in February at Manchester Magistrates' Court Shania Care-Slede has also been charged with arson offences, which she has denied and is to go on trial over in May Wilde and Eyre are also charged with possession of class B drugs (cannabis) The reservoir was reopened to the public for the first time on 27 August

NHS leaders are urging everyone eligible to book their vaccine as soon as they are invited to help reduce demand on services at the busiest time of year Health officials warn winter illnesses, including flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), can be "very serious" for vulnerable people. Vaccination is the "best way to reduce the risk of becoming seriously unwell", they add The NHS says more than two million flu jabs were delivered in the North West last year. Around four million people in the region will be eligible for the flu vaccine this year Pregnant women and children will be offered the flu vaccine from September 1, while older adults, people in care homes, people clinically at risk and health and social care workers will be eligible from October 1

title: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night

evidence_packet.title: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night
evidence_packet.lead: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed
evidence_packet.summary: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Tameside's mystery discharge pouring down road for 18 months 'may be affecting public health' Tameside Council and the Environment Agency are investigating Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 05:56, 03 Sep 2026 Updated 06:43, 03 Sep 20 Locals have spoken out about their concerns as they claim a mystery 'leak' on a road in Tameside has been causing a 'major health hazard' for more year and a half. And the Environment Agency told the MEN the contamination may be affecting public health In correspondence sent to the Manchester Evening News , an anonymous local resident who claimed to be speaking on behalf of the local community, said a leak had been 'continuously discharging' down Alt Hill Lane in Ashton-under-Lyne for more than 18 months The resident, who said they feared it may be sewage, said the issue had been reported last year but alleged that 'absolutely no action has been taken to isolate the biohazard or protect the public.' They said the main area affected was near the old railway bridge and entrance to the public bridleway on the rural road which sits on the border of Tameside and Oldham The path is a popular route for walkers, dog walkers, children and cyclists and recently it has been 'impossible to cross the road to the opposite path entrance without walking through it' they said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS NHS issues 'serious' flu warning as virus could strike earlier than usual this winter The warning comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 21:05, 02 Sep 2026 Vi Health officials have urged millions of people across the North West to protect themselves against winter viruses as the NHS warns flu could strike earlier than usual this winter It comes after last year's flu season peaked much sooner than expected, putting pressure on NHS services. NHS leaders are urging everyone eligible to book their vaccine as soon as they are invited to help reduce demand on services at the busiest time of year Health officials warn winter illnesses, including flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), can be "very serious" for vulnerable people. Vaccination is the "best way to reduce the risk of becoming seriously unwell", they add The NHS says more than two million flu jabs were delivered in the North West last year. Around four million people in the region will be eligible for the flu vaccine this year Pregnant women and children will be offered the flu vaccine from September 1, while older adults, people in care homes, people clinically at risk and health and social care workers will be eligible from October 1

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Marathon 'Four of our family members were diagnosed with cancer in four years - we had to do something' 'The hard work we're doing is nothing compared to what they've been through' Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 18:40, 02 Sep 2026 A couple who saw four of their close family members diagnosed with cancer in just four years are running 12 half marathons in 12 months to raise money for The Christie Charity after seeing first-hand the impact of its care Deb and Alex Beachell, originally from Manchester , will take on the ASICS Manchester Half Marathon this October as part of their challenge, having already completed eight races so far Deb and her wife Alex decided to take on the challenge after four members of their family, Alex’s mum and stepdad, as well as Deb’s dad and brother, were diagnosed with cancer over the last four to five years The couple, who met at Manchester Pride 20 years ago and have been married for 13 years, say they want to give something back after The Christie's care helped to give their family the all clear View 3 Images The pair said the run in Llandudno was particularly special as both their parents have always visited the town (Image: Deb and Alex)

evidence_packet.lead: Transport Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig to spend £60m fixing potholes across the city-region The major cash injection will be distributed across the 10 Greater Manchester councils Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 18:21, 02 Se Today (Wednesday, September
evidence_packet.summary: Transport Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig to spend £60m fixing potholes across the city-region The major cash injection will be distributed across the 10 Greater Manchester councils Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 18:21, 02 Se Today (Wednesday, September
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig to spend £60m fixing potholes across the city-region The major cash injection will be distributed across the 10 Greater Manchester councils Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 18:21, 02 Se Today (Wednesday, September 2), Bev Craig watched on as resurfacing work started on Trevor Road in Eccles . Her £60m Pothole Fund will go towards repairing around 125km of road in a big effort to tackle the pesky pothole problem The recently elected GM mayor believes this will increase the safety and reliability of the highways network, not just for cars, but for buses, trams and cyclists Sorting out potholes formed part of her mayoral manifesto when campaigning to replace her predecessor, Andy Burnham . Ms Craig pointed out she didn’t need to hear about potholes on the doorstep, she could see the problem with her own eyes when travelling around the city-region Ms Craig said: “I’m investing in making sure our roads are modern, up to standard and getting rid of those potholes. The £60m Pothole Fund is going straight to councils, who will help us do that View 4 Images Bev Craig, mayor of Greater Manchester, stood on Trevor Road in Eccles (Image: TfGM)

Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 18:13, 02 Sep 2026 View 3 Images ( A Salford councillor is plan
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford The councillor planning to take his own council to court in fight for greenbelt land The council approved development on the land next to RHS Bridgewater. Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 18:13, 02 Sep 2026 View 3 Images ( A Salford councillor is planning to challenge the local authority over the controversial decision to approve hundreds of new houses on former greenbelt. Peel Land were given the green light to build 282 ‘high-quality’ homes on land around the RHS Bridgewater in Boothstown in July The controversial decision left people in the area angered and upset. Locals claim the surrounding roads are already ‘at breaking point’ with congestion Conservative councillor Bob Clarke has launched a fundraiser on the community’s behalf to cover legal costs to haul the decision in front of a court of law. More than £14,000 has been raised for the judicial review in under a week, almost a third of the total predicted cost of ar Coun Clarke told the LDRS : “I’m not against housebuilding. But this is about the infrastructure of the entire area, which isn’t ready for that amount of people. It’s not just the roads, it’s the schools, doctors, dentists View 3 Images The land next to the RHS Bridgewater. (Image: Copyright Unknown)

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major update has revealed a surprising new plan for a historic Stockport library that’s been shut for more than a year Stockport Central Library has been closed since May 2025 after maintenance works and repairs had to be carried out in the building. It has remained shut ever since despite petitions and calls for it to reopen Library services in Stockport town centre have since been operating out of the massively popular Stockroom in the Merseyway Shopping Centre. This has had more than one million visitors in a year However the library’s likely future has been revealed after Reform councillor Shaun Regan put in a Freedom of Information request to the local authority He said he had ‘been pressing the council for clear answers’ in a Facebook post because the public ‘deserve to know what is happening to one of our most important public buildings’

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Wigan blackmailer faces jail over torrent of vile abuse and threats sent to MPs over Palestine Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan, sent threats and blackmail messages to high-profile MPs including Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secreta A Wigan man bombarded Health
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Wigan blackmailer faces jail over torrent of vile abuse and threats sent to MPs over Palestine Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan, sent threats and blackmail messages to high-profile MPs including Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secreta A Wigan man bombarded Health Secretary Yvette Cooper and ex-Foreign Secretary Sir James Cleverly with a torrent of vile abuse over the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The MPs, plus former Business Secretary Peter Kyle, were left offensive emails and voice mails at their constituenc Over a three-month period, Adrian Price, 57, from Wigan , threatened harassment, made ''defamatory references'' and used ''highly abusive language'' about the MPs. He is also said to have used blackmail in his messages Sir James who quit the shadow cabinet at the weekend to run for London mayor and Labour minister Mr Kyle who served in Sir Keir Starmer's Government before being dismissed by Andy Burnham in July provided victim personal statements about the abuse Prosecutors are currently awaiting a similar statement from Ms Cooper who was previously subjected to a death threat from another social media user not linked to Mr Price. The Speaker of the House of Commons Sir Lyndsay Hoyle has also given prosecutors an ''impactful'' statement At Wigan Magistrates' Court Price pleaded guilty to three charges of sending by public communication network an offensive, indecent, obscene or menacing message or matter

evidence_packet.summary: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: OIdham council responds to questions around nightmare road where 125 illegal cars were spotted in one night Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars were parked illegally from 1pm to 8pm at night Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Rep Oldham Council has revealed how many fines have been paid on a road that turns into a ‘nightmare’ because people flout the rules. The Manchester Evening News understands issues are still ongoing despite enforcement action Waterloo Street in Oldham cuts through the centre of the suburb of Glodwick but in recent months, it’s been the centre of a debate as cars park repeatedly on double yellow lines, roads are blocked, and the pavements are taken over. Videos posted online have claimed up to 125 cars When the Manchester Evening News went to visit the road in August, multiple cars could be seen parking on the double yellow lines along the entire length and one man said: “People here do not give a s***’. Cars could also be seen parked on grass verges too damaging a nearby green Rafit Hussain, a local business owner and chairman of local political party the Oldham Group, said the lack of public transport links was making the issue worse and called for more awareness and education He also said: “The traffic wardens need to do their job. It’s simple. They are not doing a good job with it.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport boss speaks amid chaos as new bin rule which nobody was told about is put in force One Stockport councillor said the controversy was 'a heck of a way to get a lot of feedback from people in a very short space of time' Comments News Stockport council's deputy boss faced questions for the first time after 'Binlid-Gate' sent collections into chaos last month Towards the end of July, Stockport council began enforcing a long-standing rule around not collecting any bins that had the lids open. The local authority said this was to ensure the safety of bin crews based on manufacturer guidance However, council officers appeared to not tell anyone the change had taken place, even top councillors. As the public did not know about the enforcement, hundreds of bins were not collected prompting major backlash Those issues appear to have largely been resolved while the council has acknowledged it did fail to tell people in advance and apologised . Last week, the council's Liberal Democrat-administration announced major changes are coming with more collections to start later this year From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts WKD thug erupts in fury at Manchester Walkabout bouncer's refusal as he launches sudden, vicious attack The alcopop thug launched his rage-fuelled attack when he was told he couldn't take his drink outside Comments News Chris Slater Senior Repo A thug swung a knife outside a bar in the Printworks after being told he couldn’t take his drink outside Wiktor Kuca, 21, erupted in fury and headbutted a doorman at Walkabout after being stopped with a bottle of WKD Just weeks earlier he had been part of a vicious attack on two men after a row over a drink at a pub in Eccles , a court heard. evidence_packet.lead: The University of Manchester Andy Burnham backs MEN campaign to save Jodrell Bank as our petition tops 10,000 signatures Funding cuts threaten the future of the observatory's iconic and much-loved Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope News John Scheerhout C A petition launched by the M
evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Andy Burnham backs MEN campaign to save Jodrell Bank as our petition tops 10,000 signatures Funding cuts threaten the future of the observatory's iconic and much-loved Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope News John Scheerhout C A petition launched by the M
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Andy Burnham backs MEN campaign to save Jodrell Bank as our petition tops 10,000 signatures Funding cuts threaten the future of the observatory's iconic and much-loved Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope News John Scheerhout C A petition launched by the Manchester Evening News to save space science at Jodrell Bank has now been signed by more than 10,000 people in just five days. And tonight our campaign has been endorsed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham We began our campaign to save space science at Jodrell Bank in late July and by this evening (Wednesday, September 2) our petition had been signed by 10,219 people Funding cuts threaten the working future of the observatory's iconic and much-loved Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope SIGN THE MANCHESTER EVENING NEWS CAMPAIGN HERE Today Prime Minister Andy Burnham emphasised again he was determined to save the observatory a day after he vowed to do so in Parliament

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Breightmet Bolton school goes into lockdown after reports of a man with a knife nearby Staff locked the doors of St Catherine's Academy in Breightmet, Bolton, at around 2.45pm today Comments News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 20:09, 02 Sep 2026 Updat A school went into lockdown today after reports that a man was seen with a knife on a nearby road Staff locked the doors of St Catherine's Academy in Breightmet, Bolton , at around 2.45pm today (Wednesday, September 2) after learning of reports of a man with a knife on nearby New Lane Parents were sent an alert confirming that the school had begun an 'invacuation' where all external doors were locked within three minutes of the report. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig to spend £60m fixing potholes across the city-region The major cash injection will be distributed across the 10 Greater Manchester councils Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 18:21, 02 Se Today (Wednesday, September 2), Bev Craig watched on as resurfacing work started on Trevor Road in Eccles . Her £60m Pothole Fund will go towards repairing around 125km of road in a big effort to tackle the pesky pothole problem The recently elected GM mayor believes this will increase the safety and reliability of the highways network, not just for cars, but for buses, trams and cyclists Sorting out potholes formed part of her mayoral manifesto when campaigning to replace her predecessor, Andy Burnham . Ms Craig pointed out she didn’t need to hear about potholes on the doorstep, she could see the problem with her own eyes when travelling around the city-region Ms Craig said: “I’m investing in making sure our roads are modern, up to standard and getting rid of those potholes. The £60m Pothole Fund is going straight to councils, who will help us do that View 4 Images Bev Craig, mayor of Greater Manchester, stood on Trevor Road in Eccles (Image: TfGM)

Comments News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 18:13, 02 Sep 2026 View 3 Images ( A Salford councillor is planning to challenge the local authority over the controversial decision to approve hundreds of new houses on former greenbelt. Peel Land were given the green light to build 282 ‘high-quality’ homes on land around the RHS Bridgewater in Boothstown in July The controversial decision left people in the area angered and upset. Locals claim the surrounding roads are already ‘at breaking point’ with congestion Conservative councillor Bob Clarke has launched a fundraiser on the community’s behalf to cover legal costs to haul the decision in front of a court of law. More than £14,000 has been raised for the judicial review in under a week, almost a third of the total predicted cost of ar Coun Clarke told the LDRS : “I’m not against housebuilding. But this is about the infrastructure of the entire area, which isn’t ready for that amount of people. It’s not just the roads, it’s the schools, doctors, dentists View 3 Images The land next to the RHS Bridgewater. (Image: Copyright Unknown)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The family-run 'Bistro' and drug dealing racket where customers ordered cocaine over WhatsApp Owner of the Village Bistro in Bury, Rezart Balesi, is due to be sentenced tomorrow, alongside his brother, his son and five others Comments News Amy A 'close-knit' family who ran a once-successful restaurant are now facing lengthy jail terms for their part in a drug dealing racket Two brothers, a son and five others were involved in the running of a drugs line, in which customers would get in touch to order cocaine through WhatsApp or social media Members of the group reported to head of the family, and owner of the Village Bistro in Bury , Rezart Balesi. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major update has revealed a surprising new plan for a historic Stockport library that’s been shut for more than a year Stockport Central Library has been closed since May 2025 after maintenance works and repairs had to be carried out in the building. It has remained shut ever since despite petitions and calls for it to reopen Library services in Stockport town centre have since been operating out of the massively popular Stockroom in the Merseyway Shopping Centre. Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Tatton Estate has insisted it is not promoting an 11,000-home scheme at Ashley and that all land north of the M56 has now been taken out of Cheshire East’s Call for Sites process - despite campaigners publishing a March letter in which the Estate In a 31 March 2026 letter found by Keep Ashley Green and seen by Altrincham Today , consultants acting for the Estate said land submitted in 2024 - including sites north of the M56 - was “still available”, and that work had identified longer-term potential for around 11,000 homes But Pete Crowther, chief executive of Tatton Estate, said the March letter referred back to the earlier 2024 submission “ As previously stated , the March document presented the vision for approximately 1,070 homes," he said. evidence_packet.summary: The family are Altrincham FC season ticket holders Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Lois (second right) with husband Ollie and kids Imogen and Jacob A local mum of two is fighting for her life in hospital after a liver transplant that almost killed her Lois Kinder, 44, was rushe
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family are Altrincham FC season ticket holders Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Lois (second right) with husband Ollie and kids Imogen and Jacob A local mum of two is fighting for her life in hospital after a liver transplant that almost killed her Lois Kinder, 44, was rushed to hospital in mid-July after becoming critically ill with acute liver failure. Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The blaze at Dove Stone reservoir, near Greenfield, Saddleworth, Greater Manchester, broke out on 11 July and was declared a major incident by the fire service. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mohammed Khalil Nadir, from Middlesborough, was found guilty of possessing articles for a terrorist purpose and disseminating terrorist publications after a trial at Leeds Crown Court in June Nadir, who had researched the Manchester synagogue attack, was arrested in October 2025 following an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing North East (CTPNE) It said he shared terrorism guides and propaganda online and regularly used chat rooms to promote violence and martyrdom The jury heard how Nadir had researched the vest worn by Jihad Al-Shamie during the Heaton Park Synagogue attack , before placing an order for a similar vest When it arrived he added 500 steel ball bearings to his online shopping basket, the hearing heard He recorded a video of himself wearing the vest, modified with a fake wire and trigger, and overlaid the sound of an explosion before sharing it on Telegram

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Garry Bridges is set to be appointed as the new Leader of Manchester City Council at a special meeting this week (Thursday 3 September, 6pm) Cllr Bridges succeeds Cllr Bev Craig, who was elected as Greater Manchester Mayor in July, having previously served as statutory Deputy Leader since 2024. Subject to confirmation at the full Council meeting, he will take up the political leadership of the Council The Leader has ultimate responsibility for setting the long-term vision for the Council at the heart of Manchester’s ongoing inclusive growth, leading a team of Executive (Cabinet) members. He will represent the Council – and the city – at regional, national and international lev Cllr Bridges’ political priority has been ensuring that Manchester’s young people have the best start in life and have the opportunities, through work and skills, to share in the city’s success Prior to becoming Deputy Leader in 2024, Cllr Bridges had held the position of Executive Member for Children and Schools and overseen significant improvements across children’s services – which are now rated Outstanding by Ofsted. This included championing free school meals durin His commitment has been accentuated by his role as a parent to two toddlers, a daughter (aged three) and a son (aged four.)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.title: What could greater devolution mean for Manchester's tech ecosystem? | Manchester Digital
evidence_packet.lead: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No
evidence_packet.summary: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No
evidence_packet.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. It should mean earlier engagement

Manager Michael Carrick oversaw a significant midfield rebuild, while the club also planned for the future by snapping up several top prospects United needed to strengthen and add depth to their squad, having finished third and qualified for the Champions League without having to contend with a European campaign last term. The spectre of Casemiro’s departure in midfield loomed large over United after his stellar final ye The Reds chose to address Casemiro’s exit and an injury to Manuel Ugarte by signing three midfielders . Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba all bring different qualities to Carrick’s side, with Kobbie Mainoo also vying for a starting spot Looking to the future, United recruited goalkeeper Kit Margetson, midfielder Cristian Orozco and winger Tynan Thompson as academy prospects. Meanwhile, Karl Darlow arrived as an experienced backup to Senne Lammens. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
